@MartinHjelmare Is this approach OK? I didn't use try_connect because of 2 reasons. 
1. it requires the TV switched on.
2. Only case we can have a port = None in config entry is for entries created before version 0.107. And prior that version only port 8001 was supported my samsungtv component
If code is OK I'll add tests.

We could add a migration for old config entries. In that case implement `async_migrate_entry` in the component module.

Config entries that fails to migrate due missing port and TV being off will not load.
@MartinHjelmare we can always improve it later in a new PR. Just let me know

review_comments: What if the default port doesn't work?

Sorry I don't understand your question. As I said: 0.106 do currently support only websocket TVs running on port 8001. All current config entries have port = None. Port None = port 8001.
If a TV requires port 8002 it's currently not supported so there are no config entries.
Default port applies only to currently supported websocket Samsung TVs. That are all running on port 8001.
If default port is not running... TV is broken ;-)
Shouldn't we check if the port is missing or `None` in the config entry? That should be the single source of thruth.

I don't understand your question sorry. 
For legacy devices the port is and was none. Port is now required  only for websocket devices (it was none before my PR). 
I can make here a simple test (set port to 8001 if method is websocket and port none) before creating the Bridge. Is this what you are asking now? 

PS: IMHO my first single line commit was the best solution... Simple yet effective
